papers.title: MEO: Mining Reliable Expert Signals for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks
papers.summary: The operation of next-generation wireless networks increasingly hinges on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize critical network decisions. Offline RL trains agents using accessible datasets and thus eliminates costly online interactions, rendering it particularly advantageous in dynamic wireless environments that demand low latency and high safety. However, its capability remains under-explored in wireless settings, where offline data are often limited and subject to partial observability. papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) remains a central optimization framework in machine learning. Although RL agents can converge to optimal solutions, the definition of ‘optimality’ depends on the environment's statistical properties. The Bellman equation, central to most RL algorithms, is formulated in terms of expected values of future rewards. However, when ergodicity is broken, long-term outcomes depend on the specific trajectory rather than on the ensemble average. papers.title: TREX: Trajectory Explanations for Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated its ability to solve complex decision-making problems in a variety of domains, by optimizing reward signals obtained through interaction with an environment. However, many real-world scenarios involve multiple, potentially conflicting objectives that cannot be easily represented by a single scalar reward. Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) addresses this limitation by enabling agents to optimize several objectives simultaneously, explicitly reasoning about trade-offs between them. papers.title: Learning stable in-grasp manipulation in a non-dropping action space
papers.summary: Traditionally, dexterous manipulation controllers are designed using analytic models constrained by strong assumptions about the hand and the objects being manipulated. Reinforcement learning (RL) has become another common approach in which skills are explored openly in an end-to-end manner but is inefficient because of unnoticeable instability and conflicts in learning objectives. papers.summary: This paper introduces a novel gripper interface designed to improve task demonstration in robot learning by providing a hardware- agnostic solution for capturing gripper-state information. papers.summary: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. papers.summary: In reinforcement learning, we typically aim to optimize the expected value of the sum of rewards an agent collects over a trajectory. papers.title: Distributed Collaborative Positioning through ISAC for GPS-Denied Robotic Swarms
papers.summary: Robotic swarms in GPS-denied environments require accurate position and velocity in real-time for all nodes, without external infrastructure or centralized control. Existing positioning approaches, including collaborative positioning, fail because of non-scalable (O(N2)) measurement overhead or centralized architectures that cannot keep pace with high-mobility swarms. papers.title: Towards Agile and Active Scene Update for Embodied Space Exploration: A WiFi-Guided Approach
papers.summary: Timely scene updating is essential for embodied agents operating in dynamic indoor environments. While cameras and LiDAR are effective for high-fidelity reconstruction and verification, relying on them alone for long-term maintenance is costly, since robots must repeatedly revisit large areas to rediscover relatively sparse changes. papers.summary: This study proposes an automated eddy current inspection technology to address the challenges in detecting subsurface cold-shut defects in aero-engine turbine blades. papers.summary: This work presents a soft finger that combines pneumatic actuation, variable stiffness, and embedded sensing and was designed, simulated, and experimentally tested. papers.summary: Underwater optical imaging is inevitably degraded by particle scattering and wavelength-dependent absorption, which jointly cause image blur, low contrast, and color casts. These optical degradations impose three critical requirements on underwater image enhancement for robotic vision systems: accurate extraction of local details, effective modeling of global scene structure, and real-time processing. papers.summary: In edge robotics, the deployment of computer resource-intensive AI models remains a pivotal challenge.
